buttonLabel: "Explore wildlife watching on a route through Brazil and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  In this selection of journeys through Brazil and Uruguay, wildlife observation primarily takes place in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands, as part of an eight-country, 32-day tour. The island section includes a marine excursion along one of two routes. Brazil's Iguaçu provides waterfall views, while Montevideo in Uruguay is a city stop. Below we compare this journey with other nature itineraries so that a scenic excursion is not mistaken for a safari.
---

## Wildlife watching on a trip through Brazil and Uruguay

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil and Uruguay among the main countries and wildlife-watching activities within the full itinerary. On the [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), these take place in Ecuador's [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). **A “Wildlife and Safari” theme does not mean there is a safari in every country visited.**

On this 32-day trip, [Brazil](/brazil/) features Iguaçu, and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) features Montevideo on a day excursion from Buenos Aires. Day 24 includes one marine excursion: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. On either route, sea lions, iguanas and birds may be seen; the exact route is confirmed after booking and animal sightings cannot be guaranteed.

The other journeys described below are nature-oriented alternatives for comparison. To see all options regardless of theme, visit the [Brazil and Uruguay tour selection](/multi-country/brazil_uruguay/). Compare [wildlife tours involving Brazil](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/) and [Uruguay](/interests/wildlife/tours/uruguay/) by their full itineraries: wildlife activities may take place in other countries.

## The Brazilian section: Iguaçu Falls and Atlantic Forest

[Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) is the principal scenic attraction in the Brazilian portion of several itineraries. Inside the national park, visitors follow viewing walkways through lush, humid forest towards the cascades and river gorge. This is a chance to experience the Atlantic Forest ecosystem, but the excursion's main planned attraction is **the waterfall scenery**, not a guaranteed encounter with a wild animal.

For comparison, the [13-day nature route through Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) includes Iguaçu after Rio and before Buenos Aires. Travelers then cross the Río de la Plata and travel to Montevideo. The nature stop is in Brazil and on the Argentine side of the falls, not in Uruguay.

Another nature alternative is the [16-day Uruguay, Paraguay and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/). Its Brazilian finale includes Iguaçu, the Macuco Safari ride and [Parque das Aves](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) according to the day's itinerary. Macuco Safari is an attraction by the falls; its name does not indicate a wildlife-tracking safari. Visiting a managed bird park and watching animals in the wild are different experiences. For bird and nature photography, distinguish between the national park and specially managed visitor facilities.

Access to particular walkways always depends on water levels and park management. Even with a confirmed trip, it would be wrong to promise a particular viewpoint or a sighting of a specific species without up-to-date evidence.

## Uruguay: coastlines and cities rather than safaris

The [13-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) includes [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) after Colonia del Sacramento. Travelers can enjoy relaxed days by the ocean, coastal scenery, walking and rest. The published program, however, does not support a promise of specialist marine-animal observation or a dedicated birdwatching outing in Uruguay.

On the [17-day tour through Chile, Argentina, Uruguay and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), the Uruguayan stage centers on Montevideo, while the major nature experiences are in Chilean and Argentine Patagonia, at Iguaçu and on the Brazilian coast. A brief stop in the capital cannot replace several days in a nature reserve.

This is an important selection criterion. If a traveler wants to see certain birds or marine mammals **specifically in Uruguay**, it is necessary to identify the right region, season and excursion format first. These multi-country tours are designed as broader journeys; a thematic tag does not confirm a specialized wildlife excursion in Uruguay.

## Where the birds are on the Uruguay, Paraguay and Brazil route

The [16-day tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) is particularly revealing. It starts in Uruguay with Montevideo, Colonia del Sacramento, Canelones and the coast. **The day at Laguna Capitán with flamingos is in Paraguay**, in the Chaco region. After that, the route continues towards Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil.

[Laguna Capitán](/paraguay/place/laguna-capitan/) may be of interest to bird lovers, but geographically it is neither a Uruguayan nor Brazilian stop. Likewise, natural encounters in Patagonia cannot be attributed to Uruguay just because it is on the same tour.

For travelers, the distinction is useful: some routes contrast Uruguay's coastal lifestyle with Brazil's waterfalls, while others add genuine natural attractions in Paraguay or Patagonia. Compare the actual wildlife-viewing days rather than the number of countries with a nature-related label.

## Choosing a nature-focused itinerary

| Route | Where the main nature section is |
|---|---|
| 8 countries, 32 days | Galápagos: wildlife watching |
| 3 countries, 13 days | Iguaçu; Uruguay's coastline |
| 4 countries, 17 days | Patagonia and Iguaçu |
| Uruguay – Paraguay – Brazil, 16 days | Chaco, lagoons, Iguaçu |

The dynamic table below shows the current tour in this selection that includes wildlife observation. Compare the other journeys in the [nature-travel selection](/multi-country/brazil_uruguay/interests/nature/). On a multi-country tour, wildlife activities may take place outside the countries named in the selection: always check the complete itinerary and the relevant days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The [13-day journey](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) leaves ample time for Iguaçu and the Uruguayan coastline, but nature is not the focus every day. The [17-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) combines tropical landscapes with Patagonia's glaciers. The [Uruguay, Paraguay and Brazil route](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) contrasts Uruguayan cities, the arid Chaco and Iguaçu's humid forests.

If wildlife is particularly important, check whether the itinerary sets aside a dedicated activity, how many hours it lasts, whether another ticket is needed and whether it can be booked for your dates. Visiting a national park may be a major nature experience without guaranteeing an encounter with a rare species.

## Practicalities: seasons, transport and observation time

The journey crosses several climatic regions. Iguaçu is humid and often warm; Uruguay's coastline can be windier and cooler than inland areas. Patagonia or the Chaco add more pronounced contrasts. Pack protection from rain, sun and wind, and carry suitable moisture protection for camera equipment during excursions.

Travel between countries also takes time. A route between Argentina and Uruguay, for example, uses a ferry across the Río de la Plata; the longer four-country tour has flights between distant regions. We help sequence the stops and assess the practicality of additional nature excursions. Park rules, tickets, entry requirements and visiting conditions must be checked for the travel dates and each traveler's nationality.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife on trips through Brazil and Uruguay

### Can wildlife sightings be guaranteed in both countries?

No. On the 32-day program, the included island wildlife activities are in Ecuador's Galápagos. Iguaçu in Brazil is a scenic excursion, and Montevideo in Uruguay is a city visit. Sightings of particular island animals are not guaranteed either.

### Where might travelers see flamingos on the 16-day tour?

The program names Laguna Capitán in Paraguay, not Uruguay. Actual sightings depend on natural conditions and bird behavior.

### Is the tour suitable for waterfall photography?

Yes. [Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) appears on several suitable routes. Allow for humidity near the falls, walkway access and the amount of time actually allotted to the park.

### How does a trip through Uruguay differ from dedicated birdwatching?

Multi-country tours combine cities, beaches, waterfalls and nature visits. Dedicated birdwatching is organized around specific observation spots and time spent watching birds. The latter cannot be promised on these routes without separate confirmation.

buttonLabel: "Explore a journey through Chile and Colombia"
lead: >-
  Chile and Colombia come together on a major 32-day Ada Tours journey across eight South American countries. The Chilean stage links Santiago and the Atacama Desert; the Colombian stage visits Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena and Bogotá. Between them lie high-altitude Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador with the Galápagos Islands. The most important considerations include exertion at altitude, connections, climatic differences and entry rules.
---

## Chile and Colombia: which tour connects the two countries?

Our “Chile + Colombia” selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. **The confirmed route covers much more than Santiago and Bogotá:** it is the [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), scheduled for October 22 through November 22, 2026. It begins in Brazil, continues through Argentina and Uruguay, then reaches Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador, ending in Colombia.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

Travelers spend several days in Chile in early November; the Colombian leg begins on November 16. **Three other countries and a demanding high-altitude section separate the selected pair.** This route suits those who want to discover the continent in sequence. A short Chile-and-Colombia-only trip requires a different itinerary and newly agreed flights and services.

| Section | Route days |
|---|---|
| Chile | 10–12 |
| Bolivia and Peru | 13–20 |
| Ecuador | 21–25 |
| Colombia | 26–32 |

Chile and Colombia share no land border. The straight-line distance from Santiago to Bogotá says little about journey time: if the goal is to spend time in Atacama and reach Colombia's Caribbean coast, airport connections, seasonality and domestic flights are far more important.

## Three days in Chile: the capital, Atacama and the highland gateway

On Day 10, travelers fly from Buenos Aires to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The next day features a sightseeing tour of the capital, taking in the city center, historical squares, architecture and views of the Andes. This urban stage can be enjoyed at a moderate pace after an international flight.

Day 12 includes a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The town is the departure point for desert landscapes, salt flats, lagoons and the high-altitude border with Bolivia. The Chilean stage ends with travel into the next country, rather than a return to Santiago.

**Atacama calls for different clothing than coastal Colombia.** Sunny locations can be warm by day, but dry air, wind, altitude and nighttime cooling change the conditions markedly. Take closed-toe shoes, warm layers, sun protection and a practical jacket. A separate optional astronomy excursion in Atacama is charged extra in the published program and depends on viewing conditions; it should not be treated as an included activity.

Travelers chiefly interested in Chile can compare [all Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [multi-country journeys](/multi-country/) to find a program where Chile is an extended destination rather than a short segment of an eight-country itinerary.

## Colombia: why the experience changes after the Andes

The Colombian section begins with a flight from Guayaquil to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). Next are a visit to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock, city sightseeing and Comuna 13, followed by a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Cartagena is a hot Caribbean coastal city with historic forts, colorful facades and walks through the old center.

After Cartagena, the itinerary continues to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) for city excursions, followed by [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. On Day 32, travelers fly from Bogotá to São Paulo for an international connection home.

Within Colombia, the route covers **Medellín's mountain valley, the humid Caribbean coast and high-altitude Bogotá**. The weather differs enough between cities that warm clothing becomes useful again after Cartagena. This is an appealing contrast with the Chilean Atacama, but means adjusting clothing and daily habits several times.

The Colombian section is full of sightseeing and transfers. Guatapé requires a road journey and has a separate excursion day in the 32-day itinerary. Images of Medellín and Guatapé should not be mistaken for a single brief city tour.

## The most important stretch between Chile and Colombia: Bolivia's altitude

After an overnight stay in San Pedro de Atacama, the route crosses into Bolivia on Day 13. A jeep journey follows high-altitude lagoons, desert and volcanic terrain, then the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Some sections are **above 4,000 m**. Further stops include La Paz, Tiwanaku, Peru's Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu.

This is where physical demands need the closest scrutiny. Even a traveler who has no trouble sightseeing in Santiago or Medellín may experience headache, nausea or weakness after rapidly gaining altitude. The program allows for acclimatization in San Pedro de Atacama, but this does not rule out altitude sickness.

Discuss altitude tolerance and cardiovascular or respiratory conditions with a doctor before departure. Rapid ascent calls for careful monitoring of symptoms, walking pace and hydration. If a gentler itinerary is needed, Ada Tours can examine the visiting order and alternative transport, but any changes must be agreed as part of the program.

After Bolivia and Peru come Ecuador: [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) and Guayaquil. The islands have special access controls, and flights require a separate time buffer. The route from Atacama to Colombia cannot be reduced to a simple flight across the Andes.

## Air connections and borders: what to check before buying tickets

For planning purposes, this journey consists of several transport challenges. Buenos Aires to Santiago is an international flight; Santiago to Atacama includes a domestic flight through Calama. This is followed by an overland high-altitude crossing into Bolivia, a later bus stage in Peru, flights to Ecuador's islands and arrival in Colombia via Guayaquil.

The crucial question is **which flights are included in the published tour and which must be purchased separately**. The terms include domestic flights as specified in the itinerary, while international transport from the traveler's country of departure and back is excluded. Booking each leg and confirming the final cost form part of making arrangements. A general inclusion clause does not imply that every additional international connection is paid for by the operator.

With so many connections, flight duration is only part of the calculation. There is also time spent exiting the airport, passing passport control, reclaiming baggage, checking in again and traveling to hotels. When connections are on separate tickets, responsibility for missed onward flights and baggage transfers may differ from that under a through ticket.

Ada Tours helps plan the order of cities, coordinate transfers, explain border requirements and provide realistic buffers. A private, shorter Chile + Colombia trip could be planned with a start in Santiago or Bogotá, but nonstop routes and connections need to be checked for the actual dates.

## Entering Chile and Colombia as a Russian citizen: two separate procedures

**For Russian citizens with valid ordinary international passports, the Russia–Chile agreement allows tourist visits without a visa for up to 90 days within each 180-day period.** Russia's Foreign Ministry Consular Department confirms this regime. Temporary stay is registered on entry; the conditions and length of admission to Chile are set under its migration rules.

Colombia includes Russia on its official list of countries exempt from visa requirements for short stays. On arrival, however, authorities may check return tickets, accommodation, purpose of travel and electronic immigration formalities. Check-Mig requirements and carrier rules should be verified before flying, since official migration advice differs for certain passenger categories and transit circumstances.

**Chile also has a separate agricultural and sanitary control procedure.** Its SAG authority requires declaration of plant and animal products imported into the country, including food packed in luggage. Even an ordinary snack should be declared according to the applicable rules. This is distinct from visa checks and can affect airport processing time.

For the complete 32-day tour, requirements must also be checked for Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Brazil and any transit countries. Visa-free entry to Chile and Colombia **does not replace the entry requirements of the other six countries**, nor does it grant a general right to work, study or reside long-term.

Information for ordinary Russian passports was checked against official sources **on October 16, 2026**. Requirements for other nationalities and personal circumstances may differ. Before departure, confirm document validity, visas, permitted entries, medical requirements and airline rules.

## Chilean pesos and Colombian pesos: the same word, different currencies

Chile uses the Chilean peso (CLP); Colombia uses the Colombian peso (COP). These are **different currencies**, and identical numbers do not mean identical values. Between these two stages, travelers also have expenses in Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. Ecuador uses USD, so some spending is denominated directly in US dollars.

A budget is best organized around actual payments. Even with 4-star hotels and domestic flights included, personal spending, tips, additional meals, optional excursions and the international flight remain. Clarify which entry and administrative fees are covered and which are extra.

Relying on a single payment method is risky. Foreign card acceptance varies; cards issued by Russian banks may face restrictions outside Russia. Cash USD can be useful as a reserve, although local currency is often needed for everyday spending in Chile and Colombia. When exchanging money, compare the amount received, commissions and banknote requirements.

Ada Tours helps identify likely cash expenses and questions to ask the bank before departure. This does not guarantee that a specific Russian payment card will work at every terminal or that currency can always be exchanged on site.

## Weather and baggage: from Santiago's spring to the Caribbean

The Chilean leg falls in late October and early November, spring in the Southern Hemisphere. Santiago may be comfortable for city walks, but Atacama has sharper day-night temperature differences. High-altitude cold in Bolivia becomes another important factor. By late November, Colombia brings Cartagena's heat and humidity, Medellín's milder climate and cooler evenings in Bogotá.

| Area | What to prepare for |
|---|---|
| Santiago | Sunny walks and cooler evenings |
| Atacama | Wind, dry air and cold nights |
| Bolivia | Altitude, cold and intense sunshine |
| Cartagena | Heat, humidity and rain |
| Bogotá | Cool weather and possible rain |

Five separate wardrobes are unnecessary; layers work better. A light shirt and sunscreen help on the coast, fleece and wind protection in the Andean highlands, and a waterproof outer layer in changeable conditions. Bring closed-toe shoes for uneven surfaces, sun protection and a small excursion backpack.

Travel insurance needs to be assessed by its covered countries, altitude exclusions, included excursions and access to medical assistance, not simply a “Latin America” label. In 2026, Colombia's Ministry of Health highlighted yellow fever in certain risk areas; this does not mean vaccination is automatically mandatory in every city. For particular destinations and vaccinations, rely on official information and medical advice.

## When to choose the long route and when to plan just two countries

**The 32-day tour suits travelers who want the Andes, historical cities, nature parks and the Galápagos on one journey.** It covers Santiago and Atacama in Chile, and four substantial urban and natural sections in Colombia. The most demanding part lies between the two, with altitude and frequent transfers.

If you mainly want to explore [Santiago and other Chilean destinations](/chile/) slowly and then spend a week in Colombia, consider a separate journey without Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. That would be a different product with its own terms. For available programs, begin with the [Chile catalog](/chile/tour/) and [Colombia catalog](/colombia/tour/), then read the [complete 32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a short tour of Chile and Colombia only?

The confirmed active option is an eight-country, 32-day tour. A shorter two-country trip would require separate planning of route, flights, price and services.

### How many days does the current tour spend in Chile and Colombia?

The Chilean section covers Days 10–12, with a highland crossing into Bolivia on Day 13. Colombia begins on Day 26 and continues through the final Day 32.

### Is altitude sickness a concern if I am interested only in Chile and Colombia?

On **this specific tour**, yes. The route between them includes highland Bolivia at elevations exceeding 4,000 m. A different direct itinerary between major cities may have different demands, which should be assessed from its actual stops.

### Can Colombian pesos pay for both sections?

No. Chile uses CLP and Colombia uses COP. Both need their own budget, plus reserves for additional spending in intermediate countries.

### Why must food be declared when entering Chile?

The Chilean SAG authority controls plant and animal products for biosecurity. The declaration and potential inspection are separate from passport and visa procedures.

### Can I fly home immediately after the Colombian section?

The published tour includes a Day 32 flight from Bogotá to São Paulo to connect with an international flight home. Ticket conditions, re-entry rules and connection time must be checked before booking.

lead: >-
  Chile and Colombia offer contrasting experiences within a long South American tour. In Chile, the route passes Santiago and San Pedro de Atacama, the starting point for a high-altitude jeep journey into neighboring Bolivia. Colombia offers mountain panoramas around Guatapé, Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá. ## Adventures in Chile and Colombia: the itinerary on offer

The **Chile + Colombia: Adventure** selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries on the main itinerary. The main available option is the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Beginning in Brazil, it crosses Argentina and Uruguay before reaching Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Several countries and numerous excursion days separate the Chilean and Colombian stages.

**The adventure theme relates to the entire itinerary.** The most expedition-like segment is in Bolivia's highlands, with 4x4 vehicles, colorful lagoons, salt flats and an overnight stay in expedition-style accommodation. Chile serves as preparation for this crossing, while Colombia has scenic mountain roads and an excursion to El Peñón rock. The itinerary does not specify a technical ascent, a multi-day trek in the Andes or an independent expedition into Colombia's jungle.

For routes of any theme visiting both countries, see the [general Chile and Colombia selection](/multi-country/chile_colombia/). If mountain hiking is the priority, compare individual days, walking times and the availability of specialist guides.

## Chile: from Santiago to the Atacama Desert

The Chilean section starts in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). After arrival, a group tour with a Russian-speaking guide covers La Moneda, Plaza de Armas, Santa Lucía Hill and modern neighborhoods. It introduces Chile's history and urban geography before the journey moves north into harsher landscapes.

A domestic flight then takes travelers to Calama, followed by a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This desert town is surrounded by valleys and volcanic mountains and serves as a starting point for regional journeys. **The scheduled day is for transfer and acclimatization**, not compulsory trekking. A telescope-based nighttime astronomy excursion is optional and charged separately, depending on observing conditions and booking confirmation.

Altitude and dry air can affect well-being. Desert days may be hot, followed by noticeably cooler evenings. Layers, closed-toe shoes, sunscreen and water for the journey are useful. The principal physical challenges come with the high-altitude section that begins outside Chile.

## Where the off-road days begin, and why Bolivia matters

From San Pedro, the route crosses into **Bolivia**. A two-day 4x4 journey with an English-speaking guide includes Laguna Verde overlooking Licancabur, the Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geothermal area and Laguna Colorada. Other highland lagoons, Ollagüe Volcano and salt flats follow on the way to Uyuni.

Much of this route lies above 4,000 m. **Altitude sickness is possible**, even for fit travelers. Traveling by jeep with short viewpoint stops does not eliminate the effects of elevation. Anyone with medical concerns should discuss acclimatization and appropriate activity with a doctor before traveling and agree the itinerary in advance.

This illustrates why geography matters with a two-country filter: the adventure episode begins in Chile's Atacama region, but the principal high-altitude attractions lie in Bolivia. Border crossings, transport and overnight conditions are fundamental to the whole journey.

## Colombia: El Peñón rock, Guatapé and changing landscapes

The Colombian stage begins with a flight from Ecuador to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). An eight-hour outing with an English-speaking guide takes travelers to El Peñol and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). It lists a replica of the old El Peñol settlement, El Peñón de Guatapé rock, decorated streets and views of a reservoir amid green hills.

**Seeing the rock does not automatically mean climbing all the stairs to the summit.** If reaching the top is essential, confirm the condition of the stairs, tickets, restrictions and available time. The agreed excursion introduces the area's natural and cultural attractions. Guatapé offers a striking change from northern Chile's desert panoramas to the Colombian Andes' green hills.

Next come sightseeing in Medellín, [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) and a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Later are [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) with Monserrate and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) with its Salt Cathedral. These days focus on cities, architecture and history. The intensity comes from the constant changes of location and means of transport rather than strenuous sports every day.

## Comparing the Chilean and Colombian stages

| Question | Chile | Colombia |
|---|---|---|
| Main stops | Santiago and San Pedro de Atacama | Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá |
| Natural scenery | Desert and volcanic mountains, followed by Bolivian lagoons | Guatapé's green hills and reservoir; Monserrate views |
| Scheduled format | City tour, flight and acclimatization | El Peñón and Guatapé excursion, cities and museums |
| Physical demands | Main altitude risk begins on the Bolivian stage | Sightseeing; strenuous sports are not specified |

This comparison can help when selecting [adventure tours](/interests/adventure/). Travelers who want more days on trails or fewer domestic flights will need a different route or changes to a private program. The theme alone does not establish that the current tour includes safaris, jungle hikes or summit climbs.

## Preparing for a long itinerary

Logistics are essential to this 32-day tour: it involves flights, intercity drives, transfers and two days in high-altitude off-road vehicles. **The combination of altitude, temperature differences and time on the road deserves particular care.** For desert and mountain sections, take wind protection, warm layers, comfortable closed-toe shoes and sun protection. The humid Colombian coast requires lighter clothes.

Domestic flights, 4-star hotel accommodation, excursions and transfers are included according to the published terms. International flights, the optional astronomy excursion and other extra services are charged separately. Not every activity mentioned in a regional description is included in the price.

The journey visits eight countries. Passport and nationality-based entry requirements need checking for each, not just Chile and Colombia. These conditions must be reviewed for the complete journey when selecting dates and flights.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this adventure tour limited to Chile and Colombia?

No. The published itinerary has eight principal countries, including Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. The filter identifies a tour with both Chile and Colombia and an adventure component.

### Is trekking in Atacama compulsory?

The Chilean section includes a flight to Calama, a transfer and acclimatization in San Pedro. It does not specify a compulsory long hike in Chile. The high-altitude journey begins the following day in Bolivia.

### Will we climb El Peñón in Colombia?

The excursion visits the El Peñol and Guatapé area. Do not assume the staircase ascent to the top is included unless the specific conditions are separately confirmed.

### Can travelers join without expedition experience?

Most city days are conventional sightseeing excursions. However, Bolivia's highland section above 4,000 m requires serious attention to health and acclimatization even without difficult hikes.

### What Colombian stops follow Guatapé?

Medellín and Comuna 13, then Cartagena, Bogotá, Monserrate and Zipaquirá with its Salt Cathedral. These are mainly sightseeing, historical and urban visits.

lead: >-
  Traveling through Chile and Colombia reveals two different worlds within South America. In Santiago, the route visits the historic center, La Moneda Palace and Plaza de Armas. Colombia adds Medellín, Cartagena and its colonial fortifications, the museums of Bogotá and Zipaquirá's underground Salt Cathedral. These cities feature in a 32-day journey across eight countries, so their cultural attractions need to be considered within the complete program.
---

## What the Chile + Colombia cultural itinerary includes

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Chile, Colombia and a culture-and-history theme. The available [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits Santiago and the Atacama area in Chile; its Colombian section takes place at the end, with Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá.

**The two countries do not make up a separate short trip.** Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador lie between them. Nevertheless, the cultural days in Chile and Colombia have distinct themes: Santiago's urban development and political history, and Colombia's colonial Caribbean heritage, modern city culture and archaeological collections.

For either country on its own, look at [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/). The complete selection without a thematic restriction is in the [Chile + Colombia catalog](/multi-country/chile_colombia/).

## Santiago de Chile: La Moneda, the main square and Santa Lucía Hill

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide is planned. Its historical focus is La Moneda, the former mint that became the seat of government, and Plaza de Armas, the central square around which the colonial city developed.

Plaza de Armas contains the cathedral, the main post office, municipal buildings and monuments relating to Santiago's history. At Santa Lucía Hill, a city panorama shows how Santiago spreads across a valley beneath the Andes.

Modern districts such as Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia are also included. This extends the tour beyond the old center and contrasts historical administrative architecture with today's residential and business neighborhoods. It remains a general city tour; access to particular museums or closed rooms inside La Moneda must be separately confirmed if not specified in the tour conditions.

## From a cultural capital to Atacama

After Santiago, the program continues with a flight to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is another side of Chile: a small town amid desert valleys and volcanic scenery. **The main purpose of the day is the transfer and acclimatization** before Bolivia's highlands.

An evening astronomy tour can be considered separately, but it is optional and depends on observing conditions. It should not be treated as an included cultural attraction merely because northern Chile is famous for observatories.

Next, the itinerary crosses into Bolivia for an off-road trip through lagoons and desert landscapes, later visiting the monuments of ancient Tiwanaku. Those monuments are part of the **Bolivian** stage, not Chile's historical itinerary. Geography matters on multi-country trips: each monument belongs to the country where it is located.

## Medellín and Comuna 13: contemporary urban culture

The Colombian section begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A city tour after arrival includes an important stop in [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/). Its streets, steps, art spaces and murals are associated with recent history and transformations in urban life.

Comuna 13 is a lived-in neighborhood, not an open-air museum. Residents, local guides, small shopkeepers and artists all make their lives here. The history of violence and social transformation deserves sensitivity: listen to knowledgeable local people rather than relying on sensational descriptions, and respect visiting rules.

A separate excursion from Medellín visits [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñol. Its focus includes painted building facades, the history of a relocated settlement and views of the reservoir. This is a combination of culture and scenic landscapes, not a succession of museum visits.

## Cartagena: fortresses and streets of a colonial port

[Cartagena de Indias](/colombia/place/cartagena/) is a major historical stop in the Colombian section. UNESCO inscribed its port, fortifications and group of monuments on the World Heritage List in 1984. The coastal location made Cartagena a hub for Spanish trade and military routes in the Caribbean. Its defenses, bastions and fortresses explain that role more vividly than a brief historical overview.

The scheduled day includes views over the bay, the Clock Tower, Manga district, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, the historic center, San Pedro Claver Church and Santo Domingo Bastion. Walking between plazas, streets and fortresses reveals the city's commercial, defensive and religious heritage.

**One sightseeing excursion does not mean an in-depth visit to every museum and interior in Cartagena.** Travelers interested particularly in fortifications or colonial architecture should arrange additional time for selected sites. Hot and humid coastal weather calls for light clothes, drinking water and sunscreen.

## Bogotá: pre-Columbian heritage, painting and Monserrate

After Cartagena, travelers fly to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). Sightseeing in the capital begins in historic La Candelaria, followed by museums and plazas. The Gold Museum holds objects created by pre-Columbian cultures. Its exhibits illustrate metalworking skills and the ceremonial significance of metals long before the Spanish conquest.

The schedule also includes the Casa de Moneda and Botero Collection, with works by one of Colombia's best-known artists. Plaza de Bolívar brings together the cathedral, administrative buildings and sites connected with political history. A visit to Monserrate follows, offering panoramic views of the capital high in the Andes.

City museums have regular closing days. **The Gold Museum is closed on Mondays**; the Casa de Moneda and Botero Collection have their own schedules. Access to particular galleries and any changes to the day need consideration when confirming the itinerary.

## Zipaquirá: the underground Salt Cathedral

The following day is devoted to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). Its key attraction is the Salt Cathedral, constructed inside the workings of a salt mine. Underground spaces, crosses, illuminated halls and tunnels are striking because architecture and natural rock meet.

The tour is led by an English-speaking guide. This matters if you want to understand the building and its symbolism in depth. Admission is included as specified in the itinerary; extra activities offered on site should not automatically be considered paid for.

Zipaquirá is a memorable closing cultural stop: after Santiago's central squares, Medellín's street art and Cartagena's Spanish fortresses, travelers enter an unusual underground space.

**Chile offers dry highland landscapes while Colombia offers green hills and the Guatapé reservoir.** Many days in other South American countries separate the two experiences.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current relevant tour is [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). ## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama and the Andean crossing

On Day 10, after visiting other countries, travelers arrive in Santiago de Chile. The following day is devoted to city sightseeing. Day 12 includes a flight to [Calama](/chile/place/calama/) and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

San Pedro lies among desert plateaus, mountains and dry valleys. The region is known for nature excursions and stargazing. **On this specific route, however, the stop is mainly for acclimatization before Bolivia.** A nighttime astronomy tour is mentioned separately and costs extra.

A two-day 4x4 journey follows through high-altitude lagoons, salt flats and the Uyuni area. These attractions are **in Bolivia**, not Chile. They should not be counted as Chilean visits just because the journey starts in San Pedro. The published itinerary does not include a separate series of excursions to all the major natural attractions in Chilean Atacama.

For a trip with several days specifically in Atacama, explore [nature tours in Chile](/interests/nature/tours/chile/) and compare the schedules.

## Colombia: Guatapé, El Peñón and Monserrate

Following Ecuador, the tour arrives in Medellín on Day 26. The next day includes [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). Green hills surround the sprawling reservoir, and the rock offers views of the water and its islands.

The viewpoint is reached via stairs and requires some physical readiness. It is not a mountaineering trek, but it is harder than an ordinary city walk. Cloudy weather can limit the panorama.

The itinerary later passes through Cartagena and Bogotá. In the capital, a visit to [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/) offers views of the city and mountain slopes. ## Why these two countries do not form a short trip

The route passes through Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador between Chile and Colombia, with many excursions and domestic flights. You cannot turn a 32-day program into a direct Atacama–Medellín journey without redesigning logistics: dates, transport, overnight stays and the acclimatization sequence would all change.

This is suited to travelers planning **an extended South American journey** and wanting varied landscapes. A one-week visit limited to Chile and Colombia calls for a different itinerary, flights and nature excursions.

Altitude deserves special attention. After San Pedro, parts of Bolivia exceed 4,000 m. Climbing El Peñón in Colombia is different: stair climbing and ordinary physical effort rather than a high-altitude jeep crossing.

## Seasons, clothing and actual services

Atacama combines dry air, strong sun and cool nights. Guatapé is greener and more humid, and Cartagena lies in a hot coastal area. A single trip requires warm layers for high altitudes, rain protection and light clothing for cities.

The [32-day program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes group tours. The nature interest and length of the journey do not mean a personal guide is available every day. The optional astronomy tour in Chile must be distinguished from included activities.

Border and transit planning must consider **all eight countries**, not just the selected pair. Entry requirements depend on nationality. Travelers whose health may be affected by altitude should discuss the highland stages with a doctor in advance.

Other formats can be found among [Colombia nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/) and [Chile nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/chile/).
